newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif., Board considers airport plan.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif., Board considers airport plan.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., Board of Supervisors was expected on Tuesday to consider a proposal to build a commercial airport at the El Toro Marine Corps Air Station.

The board was scheduled to consider the environmental impact report for the base and three reuse options -- a commercial passenger and cargo airport, a commercial cargo and general aviation airport, as well as non-aviation uses.
After the supervisors vote Tuesday, further environmental studies would be conducted. This process could take several more years, county officials said.
The base is scheduled to be converted to civilian use by 1999.

Earlier this year, a study on future uses of the El Toro Marine Corps Air Station concluded that converting the station into an international airport would pump nearly $10 billion a year into the area's economy.
The draft environmental impact report found that an international airport facility that could serve more than 38 million passengers a year would cost $1.6 billion to build.
